browser: Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright's build v1194, the one CI installs), headless, via playwright-core 1.56.1
note: expected_http_error_console_lines are the browser's own log lines for intentionally provoked failures (revision conflicts, a rejected element, refused tokens after simulated and real API restarts, save failure, save conflict, connection resets that drop create responses, a refused token before an unconfirmed create is resent, two failed autosaves, a late autosave reply held until the page moved to a copy, an edit refused after another client moved the session, a refused token when an edit to a copy reaches a restarted service, read-only storage, a document busy behind a CLI's save lock, save replies the page never got, a copy whose first reply was dropped and whose check was answered request_in_progress, a move to the trash refused for unsaved changes, and a rename refused because the document changed elsewhere). The document-list steps search, sort, rename through the dialog, move a document to the trash after confirmation, restore it, refuse a rename whose document changed elsewhere (the list then shows it as it is, and Reload with no document open only reads the list again), and check the list at 320 px. The storage-feedback steps make documents/ read-only, hold a save lock in a CLI process (detected with a non-blocking flock probe), hold one save reply 11 s past the page's 10 s deadline, drop two save replies with a connection reset after the service answered, and answer a copy first with a dropped connection and then with request_in_progress; they check how many requests the page sent and that all carried one request ID. The steps that make documents/ or drafts/ read-only (read-only storage, the failed autosaves, and the left-open copy) are skipped when running as root, since permissions do not stop root, and are then listed in skipped_steps. edits_while_a_request_is_pending delays transactions by 400 ms. The recovery steps kill the API process with SIGKILL and start a new one. Before a kill that follows a draft discard or a copy, they wait for the page's list read that those trigger: CI run 40652695710 failed once when the kill cut that read off and the development proxy answered it 502 (a test synchronization race; the same sequence exists on main). Drawing a bond waits until the page has taken in the edit's reply: CI run 40654403437 on main failed once when the draft state still read "saved" for the revision before, so the left-open copy step made drafts/ read-only before the edit was drafted (the original's draft then lagged its document by one revision). 40-fold CPU throttling around that step reproduces the failure without the wait and passes with it. The list step makes its two documents an hour old before the rename: the recency order is the files' modification time, and WSL2's clock stepped back about 0.7 s between two writes in 2 of 8 local runs (see document-management.json). The simulated-restart step used to fail now and then (#8; 1 of 20 runs on main): a request started just as the step's one-time route was used stalled in the browser, because playwright-core 1.56.1 turns request interception off when the last page route goes away. The smoke now keeps interception on with a context-wide pass-through route, and the step waits for the retried edit's response; see browser-route-race.json. The placement step duplicates a drawing as a second scene instance, moves it with its arrow buttons, adds an atom that the page places in both instances, drags an atom in the second instance only, undoes that drag, and duplicates again, checking the graph and the first instance through the API after each step and that the third instance is copied from the last (moved) one, offset by (40, 80). The recorded-states step sets, in the inspector, three stated hydrogens and a doublet radical on a bonded carbon (drawn H3C, the hydrogens on the left because its bond leans right), attachment point 1 on the other bonded carbon, and an aromatic bond, and leaves an isolated nitrogen with inferred hydrogens (drawn as N with no count). In every placement it measures the rendered SVG: no stroke of a bond ends inside a label's getBBox, every label box lies inside the SVG view box, and no stroke collapses; it also checks the labels' and the bond's accessible names. The same drawing is checked after save, after a page reload, and after closing and reopening from storage. On the nitrogen it presses charge then query, and query then charge, with the first /transactions request held until the second press is in: no request is refused and the query atom carries no charge. editor-states.png shows the result; with this step, two runs in a row passed. This result: a local run with the Chromium build CI installs, CHEMIFREE_SMOKE_NO_SKIPS=1 and FORCE_COLOR=1; earlier runs with Google Chrome 147 passed 10 of 10 and 5 of 5. Every run writes results.json, build.log, environment.json, requests.log, api.log (--log-requests), and web.log; a failed run also writes failure.png. CI runs it in the browser job; see browser-ci.json.
